scenarios.name: East LA Urban Greening (Lower LA River)
scenarios.description: Community greening NGO expanding tree canopy and open space in disadvantaged LA neighborhoods — targets RMC / Prop 4 grants in DB.

slots.mission: Expand urban tree canopy, open space, and environmental resilience in underserved Los Angeles communities along the Lower LA River corridor.
slots.problem: East Los Angeles and Lower LA River adjacent communities average 12% tree canopy vs 25% countywide. Summer surface temperatures exceed 105°F. Disadvantaged communities lack equitable access to parks and green space.
slots.activities: 1) Plant 500 native trees and shrubs on public rights-of-way and vacant lots. 2) Restore 2 acres of riparian buffer along the Lower LA River. 3) Train 40 resident stewards in tree maintenance. 4) Conduct quarterly habitat and canopy assessments with UCLA extension partner.
slots.beneficiaries: 2,400 residents in Boyle Heights, Vernon, and Southeast LA, primarily Latino households (78%) in disadvantaged communities per CalEnviroScreen.
slots.geography: Lower Los Angeles River corridor, Boyle Heights and East LA, ZIP codes 90033, 90063, Los Angeles County, California
slots.kpis: 1) 500 trees/shrubs planted by month 18. 2) 2 acres riparian habitat restored. 3) 70% 1-year plant survival. 4) 40 trained stewards certified. 5) 15% reduction in peak afternoon temperature at 8 monitoring sites.
slots.sustainability: LA County Parks adopts ROW maintenance. Steward network continues via Eastside Green Coalition ($15,000/year). Pursue RMC Prop 4 follow-on funding for phase 2.
slots.org_capacity: Founded 2016; restored 1,200 trees across South LA with 82% survival. ED is ISA-certified arborist. Partners: UCLA Extension, Eastside Green Coalition, local RMC stakeholders.

scenarios.name: CA Library Community Literacy Program
scenarios.description: Public library district running collaborative literacy and community impact programs — targets LSTA Community Impact Grants in DB.

slots.mission: Expand equitable access to literacy, digital skills, and community learning programs through California public libraries.
slots.problem: In Riverside County, 42% of adults struggle with basic literacy and 28% of households lack reliable broadband. Rural branches serve communities 20+ miles from workforce training centers.
slots.activities: 1) Deliver 3x/week adult literacy tutoring at 5 library branches. 2) Launch bilingual family literacy nights (English/Spanish). 3) Distribute 800 take-home literacy kits. 4) Partner with local schools for after-school reading mentors.
slots.beneficiaries: 1,200 adults and 600 K-5 students across 5 library branches; 70% low-income; 55% Latino; includes rural Coachella Valley communities.
slots.geography: Riverside County, California — Coachella, Indio, and Mecca library branches
slots.kpis: 1) 75% of adult learners improve ≥1 literacy level within 12 months. 2) 600 students attend after-school reading sessions. 3) 800 kits distributed. 4) 250 families attend literacy nights. 5) 85% average program attendance.
slots.sustainability: County library general fund commits $25,000/year. Friends of the Library annual gala raises $12,000. Volunteer tutor pipeline of 45 active tutors.
slots.org_capacity: Library system serves 1.5M residents; 2019-2024 literacy pilot reached 2,100 adults. Program lead is credentialed reading specialist. Partners: CA State Library, local school districts, United Way Inland Empire.

scenarios.name: Baldwin Hills Community Climate Resilience
scenarios.description: Community nonprofit serving disadvantaged LA neighborhoods — targets Baldwin Hills Conservancy consolidated grants in DB.

slots.org_name: South LA Climate and Community Alliance
slots.mission: Build climate resilience and community wellbeing in disadvantaged Los Angeles neighborhoods through parks, green infrastructure, and resident leadership.
slots.problem: Baldwin Hills and adjacent South LA communities face extreme heat, limited park access, and legacy pollution burdens. Fewer than 3 acres of parkland per 1,000 residents in target neighborhoods.
slots.activities: 1) Develop 1.5-acre community green space with native landscaping and shade structures. 2) Train 25 resident climate ambassadors. 3) Host quarterly community resilience workshops. 4) Coordinate with Baldwin Hills Conservancy on habitat connectivity.
slots.beneficiaries: 3,100 residents in Baldwin Hills, View Park, and Leimert Park; 85% disadvantaged community members; 62% Black, 22% Latino households.
slots.geography: Baldwin Hills, View Park-Windsor Hills, and Leimert Park, Los Angeles County, California
slots.kpis: 1) 1.5 acres green space completed by month 15. 2) 25 certified climate ambassadors. 3) 600 residents attend workshops. 4) 20% increase in park utilization. 5) Document 10°F shade temperature reduction at peak hours.
slots.sustainability: LA County Parks maintenance agreement for completed green space. Ambassador network sustained through existing CBO coalition ($18,000/year in-kind). BH Conservancy partnership for phase 2 habitat links.
slots.org_capacity: Operating since 2018; completed 4 community greening projects in South LA. ED has 12 years environmental justice organizing experience. Partners: Baldwin Hills Conservancy, Community Coalition, LA County Public Health.
